acceptance: No package under go/internal/cli declares a package-level atomic Deps pointer, pinned by a guard test that scans go/internal/cli
TestRunCI_DocsTests and the inboxcmd tests run with t.Parallel
go test -race -count=1 passes for landcmd, inboxcmd and every other changed cli package
fix: Thread the Deps value from the RunX verbs to the helpers as a parameter or a receiver, and remove the package-level atomic, in the two packages that have it on main: go/internal/cli/landcmd/deps.go and go/internal/cli/inboxcmd/deps.go. Then remove the per-package serial guards and the TestMain installers, because no test can swap another test deps.
summary: On 2026-11-24 two order-dependent test flakes on main ejected boundary PRs: inboxcmd (nil deps, fixed by a TestMain in #1759) and landcmd (TestPRMergeJourney_UpdateBranchTrainWithAPendingNewHead got an empty stdout, 1 in 15 race runs; it ejected PR 1746). Both have one root: each verb package keeps `current atomic.Pointer[Deps]`, its RunX entry point runs `current.Store(&deps)`, and helpers read `host()`. A parallel test that calls RunX with partial deps replaces the deps of every other running test. The landcmd fix made the swapping test serial and added a guard test (host_swap_serial_test.go). The guard covers one package, and the global stays.
title: CLI verb packages pass their host deps down, instead of storing them in a process-wide atomic
